_meta.source_api: NASA NeoWs (Near Earth Object Web Service) — feed endpoint
_meta.notes: Maps NeoWs field names to display info, matching the same structure as data/exoplanet-column-map.json for consistency across tools. Each row in data/asteroids.json represents one CLOSE-APPROACH EVENT, not one asteroid — the same asteroid can appear on multiple rows if it makes more than one close approach within the tracked window. `category` groups fields in detail views/tooltips. `precision` is a suggested decimal-place count for display. `nullLabel` is what to show when a value is missing. `siConversion` (where present) drives the hover-icon tooltip the same way it does in the exoplanet tool.

is_potentially_hazardous.label: Potentially Hazardous
is_potentially_hazardous.tooltip: NASA classifies an asteroid as potentially hazardous if it's larger than ~140 m AND its orbit brings it within 7.5 million km of Earth — a broad screening threshold, not a prediction of impact.

absolute_magnitude_h.label: Absolute Magnitude (H)
absolute_magnitude_h.tooltip: A measure of how bright the asteroid would appear from a fixed reference distance. Lower numbers mean a larger object — this is the main way asteroid sizes are estimated, since a direct diameter measurement is rarely available.

estimated_diameter_km_min.label: Estimated Diameter (min)
estimated_diameter_km_min.tooltip: Lower bound of the estimated diameter range. Actual asteroid diameters are usually inferred from brightness and are genuinely uncertain — hence a range rather than one number.

estimated_diameter_km_max.label: Estimated Diameter (max)
estimated_diameter_km_max.tooltip: Upper bound of the estimated diameter range.

close_approach_date.label: Close Approach Date
close_approach_date.tooltip: Date of this specific close approach to Earth.

close_approach_date_full.label: Close Approach Date & Time
close_approach_date_full.tooltip: Full date and time (UTC) of closest approach.

relative_velocity_km_s.label: Relative Velocity
relative_velocity_km_s.tooltip: Speed of the asteroid relative to Earth at closest approach.

miss_distance_km.label: Miss Distance
miss_distance_km.tooltip: Closest distance between the asteroid and Earth's center during this approach.

miss_distance_lunar.label: Miss Distance (lunar)
miss_distance_lunar.tooltip: Miss distance expressed in multiples of the average Earth-Moon distance (≈384,400 km) — often a more intuitive scale than raw kilometers.

orbiting_body.label: Orbiting Body
orbiting_body.tooltip: The body this close approach is measured relative to — almost always Earth for objects in this tracker.

nasa_jpl_url.label: JPL Reference
nasa_jpl_url.tooltip: Link to this object's full record on NASA JPL's Small-Body Database.
